title.zh: 卷六 本紀第六 明帝
title.en: Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Ming of Southern Qi
title.raw: 卷六 本紀第六 明帝 Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Ming of Southern Qi

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第六 本紀第六

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 6, Annals 6
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 6, Annals 6

sentences.zh: 高宗明皇帝諱鸞，字景栖，始安貞王道生子也。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Emperor Ming, taboo name Luan, style Jingshu, was a son of Prince Zhen of Shi'an, Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, canonically titled High Ancestor, bore the name Luan and the style Jingshu; he was born to Prince Zhen of Shi'an, Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 小諱玄度。

translations.literal: Childhood taboo Xuandu.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he was called Xuandu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，太祖撫育，恩過諸子。

translations.literal: Orphaned while young, the Grand Ancestor raised him and favored him beyond his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early; the Grand Ancestor brought him up and loved him more than his own children.

sentences.zh: 宋泰豫元年，爲安吉令，有嚴能之名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taizuo of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.
translations.idiomatic: Song Taizuo 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.

sentences.zh: 補武陵王左常侍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed left attendant to the Prince of Wuling but did not accept the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was named left attendant to the Prince of Wuling and declined.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，爲永世令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, he was made magistrate of Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhui 2: he was made magistrate of Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，爲邵陵王安南記室參軍，未拜，仍遷寧朔將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was made recorder on the Pacifying-South staff of the Prince of Shaoling; before he took office he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming 2: he was named recorder on the pacifying-south staff of the Prince of Shaoling; before he reported, he was moved to general who pacifies the north and administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his rank was raised to general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，遷侍中，封西昌侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor ascended the throne, Luan was transferred to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang with a fief of 1,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, he became palace attendant and was enfeoffed as marquis of Xichang with 1,000 households.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，爲持節、督郢州司州之義陽諸軍事、冠軍將軍、郢州刺史，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of Yingzhou and Yiyang in Sizhou, Champion General, and Inspector of Yingzhou, and advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 2: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，轉度支尚書，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right-Army General.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Wu's accession he became minister of revenue and also right-army general.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，遷侍中，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently Valiant-Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 1: he was made palace attendant and valiant-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 王子侯舊乘纏帷車，高宗獨乘下帷，儀從如素士。

translations.literal: Princes and marquises of old rode carriages with wrapped curtains; the High Ancestor alone rode with lowered curtains, his escort like that of a plain gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and marquises had always traveled in curtained coaches; Luan alone used lowered screens, his train no grander than a common officer's.

sentences.zh: 公事混撓，販食人擔火誤燒牛鼻，豫章王白世祖，世祖笑焉。

translations.literal: Official business was in confusion; a food vendor's carrying-fire accidentally burned an ox's nose. The Prince of Yuzhang told Emperor Wu, and the emperor laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Government was in disorder; a peddler's brazier set an ox's nose afire by mistake. The Prince of Yuzhang reported it to Emperor Wu, who only laughed.

sentences.zh: 轉爲散騎常侍、左衛將軍，清道而行，上甚悅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Irregular Cavalry Attendant and Left Guards General; he had the road cleared when he went out, and the sovereign was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He became irregular cavalry attendant and left guards general, had the streets cleared when he passed, and the throne was much pleased.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲征虜將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the second year, he went out as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he left the capital as general who conquers the barbarians and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷中領軍，常侍竝如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Central Army-inspector-in-Chief, his attendant posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became central army-inspector-in-chief, keeping his attendant titles.

sentences.zh: 五年，爲持節、監豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事、右將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs of Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, Right General, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Xiyang in Ying and Runan in Si, became right general and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 七年，爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 八年，加領衛尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was additionally made Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was also made commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉左僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was moved to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 十一年，領右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he additionally led the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he also commanded the right guards.

sentences.zh: 世祖遺詔爲侍中、尚書令，尋加鎮軍將軍，給班劔二十人。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu's deathbed will he was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was additionally made General Who Stabilizes the Army and given twenty ceremonial sword-guards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's final testament made him palace attendant and director of the masters of writing; soon he was also general who stabilizes the army, with twenty sword-bearers in his train.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，卽本號爲大將軍，給鼓吹一部，親兵五百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was promoted on his existing title to Great General and given one set of martial pipes and five hundred personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang 1: his present rank was raised to great general; he received a band of martial pipes and five hundred household guards.

sentences.zh: 尋又加中書監、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Supervisor of the Secretariat and given secretariat parity equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also supervisor of the secretariat with honors equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 郁林王廢，海陵王立，爲使持節、都督揚南徐二州軍事、驃騎大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州刺史，開府如故，增班劔爲三十人，封宣城郡公，二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin was deposed and the Prince of Hailing enthroned, Luan was made Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Yang and South Xu, Chief Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou, his secretariat office unchanged, his sword-guards increased to thirty, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng with a fief of 2,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Yulin was removed and the Prince of Hailing made emperor, Luan bore the staff with full powers, commanded Yang and South Xu, recorded the masters of writing, and took Yangzhou, keeping his secretariat seat; his guard of swords rose to thirty, and he was made duke of Xuancheng with 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 鎮東府城。

translations.literal: He garrisoned the Eastern Palace city.
translations.idiomatic: He held the eastern palace fortress.

sentences.zh: 給兵五千人，錢二百萬，布千匹。

translations.literal: He was given five thousand troops, two million in cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand soldiers, two million cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth were granted him.

sentences.zh: 九江作難，假黃皞，事寧，表送之。

translations.literal: When Jiujiang rose in revolt, he was lent the yellow battle-axe; when the affair was settled, he memorialized to return it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiujiang rebellion he was lent the yellow battle-axe; when peace returned, he submitted it back.

sentences.zh: 尋加黃皞、都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，增班劔爲四十人，給幢絡三望車，前後部羽葆鼓吹，劔履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，封宣城王，邑五千戶，持節、侍中、中書監、錄尚書並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given the yellow battle-axe, command of all armies within and without, and the post of Grand Tutor, while retaining Great General and Governor of Yangzhou; his sword-guards were increased to forty; he was given a triple-canopy carriage with pennons, martial pipes before and behind, permission to wear sword and shoes in court and enter without hastening, to be praised without having his name spoken, and a full staff of left and right chief clerks, marshals, secretariat attendants, and aides four each; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng with a fief of 5,000 households; Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Chief Recorder—all unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the yellow axe again, overall command within and without, and the grand tutorship, while keeping great general and Yangzhou; forty sword-guards, a triple-canopy coach with banners, pipes fore and aft, sword and shoes in audience, unhurried entry, praise without naming, and staffs of four chief clerks, marshals, secretariat aides, and clerks on each flank; he was made prince of Xuancheng with 5,000 households, and kept the staff, palace attendance, secretariat supervision, and chief recordership as before.

sentences.zh: 未拜，太后令廢海陵王，以上入纂太祖爲第三子，羣臣三請，乃受命。

translations.literal: Before he accepted these honors, the empress dowager deposed the Prince of Hailing and installed Luan as the Grand Ancestor's third son; the ministers begged three times before he accepted the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office, the empress dowager removed the Prince of Hailing and set Luan in the line as the Grand Ancestor's third son; only after three rounds of pleading from the court did he accept.

sentences.zh: 建武元年冬十月癸亥，卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guihai of the first year of Jianwu: he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 1, winter, tenth month, day guihai: he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「皇齊受終建極，握鏡臨宸，神武重輝，欽明懿鑠，七百攸長，磐石斯固。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The house of Qi received the mandate, established the pinnacle, holds the mirror and faces the throne; divine martial radiance shines anew, reverent brilliance is splendid; seven hundred years would be long, and bedrock thus firm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Qi took heaven's end and built the height, holding the mirror and ruling from the hall; martial spirit burns bright again, wise grace gleams; seven hundred years should stand firm as bedrock.

sentences.zh: 而王度中蹇，天階荐阻，嗣命多違，蕃釁孔棘，宏圖景曆，將墜諸淵。

translations.literal: Yet the royal measure faltered mid-course, heaven's steps met repeated blocks, the succession was often violated, and border troubles grew desperately sharp; the grand design and bright calendar were about to fall into the abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the royal way stumbled, heaven's stair met one obstruction after another, heirs were set aside, and frontier feuds bristled; the great plan and shining calendar nearly sank into the deep.

sentences.zh: 宣德皇后遠鑒崇替，憲章舊典，疇咨台揆，允定靈策，用集寶命于予一人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuande, discerning far the rise and fall, took the statutes and old canon, consulted the chief ministers, truly settled the divine plan, and gathered the precious mandate upon me alone.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuande, seeing far how dynasties turn, held to statute and ancient rule, asked counsel of the chief ministers, fixed the sacred design, and laid the precious charge on me alone.

sentences.zh: 猥以虛薄，纘承大業，仰繫鴻丕，顧臨兆民，永懷先構，若履春冰，寅憂夕惕，罔識攸濟，思與萬國播此惟新。

translations.literal: I am mean and slight, yet inherit the great enterprise; I look up to the vast blessing and down upon the myriad people; I forever recall the former foundation as if treading spring ice; from dawn I worry and at dusk I tremble, not knowing what will carry me through; I wish with all lands to spread this renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and thin as I am, I take up the great work, tie myself to heaven's vast favor, and face the million lives below; I think always of the work of old as on spring ice; worry fills my mornings and fear my nights, and I do not see the ford; I would spread this renewal through every realm.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed for all under heaven, and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven was pardoned, and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 宿衛身普轉一階，其餘文武，賜位二等。

translations.literal: Palace guards and personal attendants were each advanced one rank; all other civil and military officers received two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards and body servants each rose one step in rank; the rest of civil and military service gained two.

sentences.zh: 逋租宿責，換負官物，在建武元年以前，悉原除。

translations.literal: Overdue rents and old debts, and goods owed to government offices, incurred before the first year of Jianwu—all were wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Back rent, old arrears, and goods owed to the state before Jianwu 1 were all forgiven.

sentences.zh: 劫賊餘口在臺府者，可悉原放。

translations.literal: Surviving dependents of bandits held in the capital offices might all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Kin left from bandit gangs held in capital prisons might all be freed.

sentences.zh: 負釁流徙，竝還本鄉。

translations.literal: Those exiled for debt or crime were all sent back to their native districts."
translations.idiomatic: Debtors and criminals in exile were all returned home."

sentences.zh: 」太尉王敬則爲大司馬，司空陳顯達爲太尉，尚書令王晏加驃騎大將軍，中領軍蕭諶爲領軍將軍、南徐州刺史，皇子寶義爲揚州刺史，中護軍王玄邈爲南兖州刺史，新除右將軍張瑰爲右光祿大夫，平北將軍王廣之爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal; Minister of Works Chen Xianda was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Central Army-inspector-in-Chief Xiao Chen was made Commandant of the Guards and Inspector of South Xuzhou; the prince Bao Yi was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Central Army-protector Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; the newly appointed Right General Zhang Gui was made Right Grand Master of Splendor; Pacifying-North General Wang Guangzhi was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze, grand commandant, became grand marshal; Chen Xianda, minister of works, became grand commandant; Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, was also made general of chariots and cavalry; Xiao Chen, central army-inspector-in-chief, became commandant of the guards and inspector of South Xu; Prince Bao Yi took Yangzhou; Wang Xuanmiao, central army-protector, took South Yanzhou; Zhang Gui, newly made right general, became right grand master of splendor; Wang Guangzhi, pacifying-north general, took Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔斷遠近上禮。

translations.literal: Day yichou: an edict cut off distant and near congratulatory gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Day yichou: an edict forbade congratulatory offerings from far and near.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔「自今雕文篆刻，歲時光新，可悉停省。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: an edict said, "From now on carved ornament and seal-cut inlay, and yearly novelties in dress—let all be stopped and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingmao: an edict said, "Hereafter figured carving, seal script, and inlay, and every seasonal novelty in dress—all are to cease.

sentences.zh: 蕃牧守宰，或有薦獻，事非任土，嚴加禁斷。

translations.literal: Where frontier lords, governors, or magistrates make offerings not native to their soil, strictly forbid and cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: Where border princes, prefects, or magistrates send tribute not proper to their land, forbid it in the strictest terms."

sentences.zh: 」追贈安陸昭侯緬爲安陸王。

translations.literal: Marquis Mian of Anlu, posthumously advanced to Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, marquis of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以安陸侯子寶晊爲湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jisi: the son of the Marquis of Anlu, Bao Zhi, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day jisi: Bao Zhi, son of the marquis of Anlu, took Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「頃守職之吏，多違舊典，存私害公，實興民蠹。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lately officials in office have often violated the old statutes, kept private ends and harmed the public, and truly become parasites on the people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Of late magistrates have broken old law, served themselves and hurt the public, and become a true plague on the people.

sentences.zh: 今商旅稅石頭後渚及夫鹵借倩，一皆停息。

translations.literal: Now the merchant tax at Shitou rear ford and every levy on salt pans and leases—all are halted.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant toll at Shitou rear ford and every salt-field rent and lease—stop them all.

sentences.zh: 所在凡厥公宜，可卽符斷。

translations.literal: Everywhere, whatever such public exactions exist, cut them off at once by warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever such public levies remain, cut them off at once by order.

sentences.zh: 主曹詳爲其制，憲司明加聽察。」

translations.literal: The chief clerks shall draw up detailed rules; the censorate shall listen and investigate with clarity."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks shall draft the rules in full; the censorate shall hear cases and investigate openly."

sentences.zh: 十一月癸酉，以西中郎長史始安王遙光爲揚州刺史，晉壽太守王洪範爲青、冀二州刺史，尚書令王晏領太子少傅。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally led the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Xiao Yaoguang, prince of Shi'an and staff clerk of the west central corps, took Yangzhou; Wang Hongfan, administrator of Jinshou, took Qing and Ji; Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, also became the crown prince's junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，大司馬尋陽公王敬則等十三人進爵邑各有差。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: Grand Marshal Duke Jingze of Xunyang and twelve others were advanced in noble rank and fief, each by a different measure.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiaxu: Wang Jingze, grand marshal and duke of Xunyang, and twelve others were raised in rank and fief, each by a set amount.

sentences.zh: 詔省新林苑，先是民地，悉以還主，原責本直。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the New Forest Park; the former commoners' land was all returned to its owners, and original payments were forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict closed the New Forest Park; former peasant holdings were returned to their owners, and old dues were remitted.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，立皇子寶義爲晉安王，寶玄爲江夏王，寶源爲廬陵王，寶夤爲建安王，寶融爲隨郡王，寶攸爲南平王。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: the princes Bao Yi, Bao Xuan, Bao Yuan, Bao Yin, Bao Rong, and Bao You were enfeoffed as Princes of Jin'an, Jiangxia, Luling, Jian'an, Suizhou, and Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengchen: Bao Yi was made prince of Jin'an; Bao Xuan, prince of Jiangxia; Bao Yuan, prince of Luling; Bao Yin, prince of Jian'an; Bao Rong, prince of Suizhou; Bao You, prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔曰：「邑宰祿薄俸微，不足代耕，雖任土恒貢，亦爲勞費，自今悉斷。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: an edict said, "District magistrates receive thin salaries too small to replace farming; though tribute fixed by their soil is constant, it is still labor and expense—from now on cut it all off.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiashen: an edict said, "Magistrates' pay is thin and will not feed a household; even fixed local tribute is a burden—henceforth end it all.

sentences.zh: 」又詔「宣城國五品以上，悉與滿敘。

translations.literal: "Another edict said, "In the state of Xuancheng, all of fifth rank and above shall receive full advancement in rank;
translations.idiomatic: "A second edict said, "In Xuancheng, all of fifth rank and above shall be advanced to the full of their grade;

sentences.zh: 自此以下，皆聽解遣。

translations.literal: from this rank downward, all may be released from service.
translations.idiomatic: from that rank down, all may be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其欲仕，適所樂。

translations.literal: Those who wish to serve may take posts suited to their inclination.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to serve may take whatever post suits their wish.

sentences.zh: 」乙酉，追尊始安貞王爲景皇，妃爲懿后。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Prince Zhen of Shi'an was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, and his consort as Empress Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: Prince Zhen of Shi'an was posthumously titled Emperor Jing, and his consort Empress Yi.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以輔國將軍聞喜公遙欣爲荊州刺史，寧朔將軍豐城公遙昌爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: General Who Assists the State Duke Yaoxin of Wenxi was made Inspector of Jingzhou; General Who Pacifies the North Duke Yaochang of Fengcheng was made Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingxu: Xiao Yaoxin, duke of Wenxi and general who assists the state, took Jingzhou; Xiao Yaochang, duke of Fengcheng and general who pacifies the north, took Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔「細作中署、材官、車府，凡諸工，可悉開番假，遞令休息」。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: an edict said, "The fine-crafts central office, the arsenal, and the chariot office—all workshops may open rotating leave and pass rest in turn."
translations.idiomatic: Day dinghai: an edict said, "Fine crafts, the arsenal, and the chariot office—every workshop may rotate furloughs and rest in turn."

sentences.zh: 戊子，立皇太子寶卷，賜天下爲父後者爵一級，孝子順孫、義夫節婦，普加甄賜明揚。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who had become fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who had become a father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 表其衡閭，賚以束帛。

translations.literal: Their lanes were marked on the registers and they were given bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Their neighborhoods were posted in honor, and they were given silk.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔「東宮肇建，遠近或有慶禮，可悉斷之。

translations.literal: Day jichou: an edict said, "The eastern palace is newly founded; distant and near may wish to send congratulatory gifts—all such are cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Day jichou: an edict said, "The heir's palace is new; gifts of congratulation from far and near are forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」壬辰，以新除征虜將軍江夏王寶玄爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Day renchen: the newly appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia was made Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day renchen: Bao Xuan, newly made general who conquers the barbarians and prince of Jiangxia, took Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永明中，御史中丞沈淵表百官年登七十，皆令致仕，竝窮困私門。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan memorialized that all officials who reached seventy years should be made to retire, and that they were all in want in their private households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan urged that every official who turned seventy be retired, noting that many were destitute at home.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔曰：「日者百司耆齒，許以自陳，東西二省，猶沾微俸，辭事私庭，榮祿兼謝，興言愛老，實有矜懷。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: an edict said, "Lately the hundred offices, at advanced age, were allowed to declare themselves; the eastern and western secretariats still drew a small salary, yet they resigned affairs to their private gates and refused both honor and stipend—speaking of love for the aged, this truly stirs pity.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengzi: an edict said, "Lately elders in the hundred offices were permitted to step down; yet men in the two secretariats still drew a slender pay while they left business to their homes and refused both rank and salary—such love of age moves us to pity.

sentences.zh: 自縉紳年及，可一遵永明七年以前銓敘之科。

translations.literal: From gentry who reach that age onward, let all follow the advancement rules used before the seventh year of Yongming."
translations.idiomatic: From the gentry upward, when they reach that age, let all follow the advancement code of before Yongming 7."

sentences.zh: 」上輔政所誅諸王，是月復屬籍，各封子爲侯。

translations.literal: The princes put to death during his regency had their names restored to the imperial clan this month, and each had a son enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The princes killed in his regency were readmitted to the clan roll this month, and a son of each was made marquis.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬子，詔曰：「上覽易遺，下情難達，是以甘棠見美，肺石流詠。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day renzi: an edict said, "The ruler who looks down finds it easy to miss; the feelings below are hard to reach—thus the sweet pear was praised, and the lung-stone sang.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day renzi: an edict said, "From above one easily overlooks; grief below is hard to hear—hence the sweet pear was praised and the lung-stone hymned.

sentences.zh: 自月一視黃辭，如有含枉不申、懷直未舉者，莅民之司，竝任厥失。」

translations.literal: From now on, once a month review the yellow-file petitions; where wrongs are unredressed or the upright uncommended, the officials who rule the people shall bear their failures."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, once a month, hear the yellow-file pleas; if the wronged are not cleared or the upright not raised, the magistrates shall answer for it."

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛未，詔「京師繫囚殊死，可降爲五歲刑，三署見徒五歲以下，悉原散。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, first month, day xinwei: an edict said, "Capital prisoners sentenced to death may be reduced to five years' punishment; convict laborers in the three offices sentenced to five years or less—all pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 2, spring, first month, day xinwei: an edict said, "Capital felons under sentence of death may be reduced to five years; convicts in the three offices at five years or below—all freed.

sentences.zh: 王公以下，各舉所知。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, each shall recommend those he knows.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down, each shall name men he knows.

sentences.zh: 隨王公卿士，內外羣僚，各舉朕違，肆心極諫。

translations.literal: Following the princes, dukes, gentlemen, and inner and outer officials, each shall cite my faults and speak his mind to the limit of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Princes, dukes, ministers, and officers within and without shall each cite my faults and remonstrate without reserve."

sentences.zh: 」索虜寇司、豫、徐、梁四州。

translations.literal: The northern enemy raided the four provinces of Si, Yu, Xu, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners raided Si, Yu, Xu, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣鎮南將軍王廣之督司州征討，右衛將軍蕭坦之督徐州征討，尚書右僕射沈文季督豫州征討。

translations.literal: Day renshen: Pacifying-South General Wang Guangzhi was sent to supervise the Si campaign; Right Guards General Xiao Tanzhi was sent to supervise the Xu campaign; Right Vice Director Shen Wenji was sent to supervise the Yu campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Day renshen: Wang Guangzhi, pacifying-south general, was sent to command the Si front; Xiao Tanzhi, right guards general, the Xu front; Shen Wenji, right vice director, the Yu front.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔京師二縣有毀發墳壟，隨宜修理。

translations.literal: Day jimao: an edict said that in the capital's two counties, wherever tombs had been opened and violated, repair as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Day jimao: an edict ordered that in the capital's two counties, desecrated tombs be repaired where needed.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「食惟民天，義高姬載，蠶實生本，教重軒經。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Food is the people's heaven; its meaning was raised high in the records of Ji; silkworms are the root of life; their teaching was weighty in the canon of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict said: "Food is the people's heaven—the Book of Ji sets its meaning high; silkworms are the root of living—the canon of Xuan gives their teaching weight.

sentences.zh: 前哲盛範，後王茂則，布令審端，咸必由之。

translations.literal: The great models of former sages and the rich standards of later kings—when they issued orders and examined beginnings, all went by these.
translations.idiomatic: Sages of old and kings of later days, when they proclaimed law and weighed the start, all walked this road.

sentences.zh: 朕肅扆巖廊，思弘風訓，深務八政，永鑒在勤，靜言日昃，無忘寢興。

translations.literal: I sit in solemnity upon the high hall and think to spread wind and instruction; I deeply pursue the eight policies and forever take diligence as my mirror; in quiet speech at sunset I do not forget to rise from sleep.
translations.idiomatic: I sit stern in the high hall and mean to spread custom and teaching; I press hard on the eight duties and keep diligence as my glass; at dusk in silence I do not forget to rise from bed.

sentences.zh: 守宰親民之主，牧伯調俗之司，宜嚴課農桑，罔令遊惰，揆景肆力，必窮地利，固脩堤防，考校殿最。

translations.literal: Magistrates are the lords who draw near to the people; governors are the officers who tune custom—they should strictly examine farming and sericulture, allow no roaming idleness, measure the seasons and exert strength, exhaust the land's advantage, firmly repair dikes and dams, and assess achievement and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates are masters of the people; governors tune the folkways—they must press farming and mulberry, forbid wandering sloth, measure the seasons and spend their force, use the soil to the last, keep dikes in repair, and grade success and failure.

sentences.zh: 若耕蠶殊衆，具以名聞；

translations.literal: Where plowing and silkworms are outstanding, report them by name;
translations.idiomatic: Where tillage and silk excel, report the names;

sentences.zh: 遊怠害業，卽便列奏。

translations.literal: where roaming idleness harms the work, at once memorialize it."
translations.idiomatic: where idleness harms the task, memorialize at once."

sentences.zh: 主者詳爲條格。

translations.literal: The responsible offices shall draw up detailed regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Let the chief offices draft the rules in detail."

sentences.zh: 」乙未，虜攻鐘離，徐州刺史蕭惠休破之。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: the enemy attacked Zhongli; Inspector of Xuzhou Xiao Huixiu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiwei: northerners besieged Zhongli; Xiao Huixiu, inspector of Xu, broke them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加太尉陳顯達使持節、都督西北征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was additionally made Bearer of the Staff with full credentials and Supervisor of all northwestern campaign armies.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingshen: Chen Xianda, grand commandant, was also given the staff with full powers and command of the northwestern campaign.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: martial closure within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingyou: court and camp were placed under strict closure.

sentences.zh: 三月戊申，詔「南徐州僑舊民丁，多充戎旅，蠲今年三課。

translations.literal: Third month, day wushen: an edict said, "In South Xuzhou many old émigré householders have been pressed into the army rolls—remit this year's three levies."
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day wushen: an edict said, "In South Xu many old southern émigré households fill the army lists—forgive this year's three taxes."

sentences.zh: 」己未，司州刺史蕭誕與衆軍擊虜，破之。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: Inspector of Sizhou Xiao Dan with the massed armies struck the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiwei: Xiao Dan, inspector of Si, with the combined hosts routed the northerners.

sentences.zh: 詔「雍、豫、司、南兖、徐五州遇寇之家，悉停今年稅調。

translations.literal: An edict said, "In the five provinces of Yong, Yu, Si, South Yan, and Xu, every household that met the raid—halt this year's taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In Yong, Yu, Si, South Yan, and Xu, every home struck by the raid—stop this year's taxes.

sentences.zh: 其與虜交通，不問往罪。

translations.literal: Those who had dealings with the enemy—do not inquire into past guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Men who trafficked with the enemy—past crimes are not asked."

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，停青州麥租。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: the Qingzhou wheat levy was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingyin: Qingzhou's wheat tax was suspended.

sentences.zh: 虜自壽春退走。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew from Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners pulled back from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 甲申，解嚴。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: martial closure was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiashen: the strict closure was lifted.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己亥朔，詔「三百里內獄訟，同集京師，克日聽覽。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day jihai of the month: an edict said, "Within three hundred li, lawsuits shall all be gathered in the capital and heard on a fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, new moon jihai: an edict said, "Within three hundred li, all suits shall come to the capital and be heard on a set day.

sentences.zh: 此以外委州郡訊察。

translations.literal: Beyond that, entrust trial and investigation to the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that range, leave trial to the provinces and districts.

sentences.zh: 三署徒隸，原遣有差。

translations.literal: Convict laborers of the three offices—release with differing measures."
translations.idiomatic: Convicts of the three offices—release in graded pardon."

sentences.zh: 」索虜圍漢中，梁州刺史蕭懿拒退之。

translations.literal: The northern enemy besieged Hanzhong; Inspector of Liangzhou Xiao Yi repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners besieged Hanzhong; Xiao Yi, inspector of Liang, drove them off.

sentences.zh: 己未，以新除黃門郎裴叔業爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: the newly appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pei Shuye was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiwei: Pei Shuye, newly made gentleman of the yellow gate, was appointed inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 五月甲午，寢廟成，詔「監作長帥，可賜位一等，役身遣假一年，非役者蠲租同假限。」

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jiawu: the resting temple was completed; an edict said, "The overseers and foremen of the work may each be advanced one rank in grade; corvée laborers are to be given leave for one year; those not on corvée shall have their land tax remitted for the same period."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day jiawu: the tomb temple was finished. An edict said, "Overseers and lead hands may each rise one grade; corvée men are released for a year; those not on corvée have their land tax forgiven for the same span."

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，誅領軍將軍蕭諶、西陽王子明、南海王子罕、邵陵王子貞。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renxu: the Director of the Army Xiao Chen, Prince Ziming of Xiyang, Prince Zihan of Nanhai, and Prince Zizhen of Shaoling were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day renxu: Xiao Chen, director of the army, Prince Ziming of Xiyang, Prince Zihan of Nanhai, and Prince Zizhen of Shaoling were executed.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以右衛將軍蕭坦之爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Day yichou: Right Guards General Xiao Tanzhi was made Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day yichou: Xiao Tanzhi, right guards general, became director of the army.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛未，以右將軍晉安王寶義爲南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Right General Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an was made Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month of autumn, day xinwei: Prince Bao Yi of Jin'an, right general, took South Xu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以冠軍將軍梁王爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Day renshen: Champion General the Prince of Liang was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day renshen: the Prince of Liang, champion general, was made inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以氐楊馥之爲北秦州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: the Di chieftain Yang Fuzhi was made Inspector of North Qinzhou and Duke of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinmao: Yang Fuzhi of the Di was made inspector of North Qin and duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 八月丁未，以右衛將軍廬陵王寶源爲南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dingwei: Right Guards General Prince Bao Yuan of Luling was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day dingwei: Prince Bao Yuan of Luling, right guards general, took South Yan.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以新除輔國將軍申希祖爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: the newly appointed Supporter-of-the-State General Shen Xizu was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengxu: Shen Xizu, newly made supporter-of-the-state general, was appointed inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，改封南平王寶攸爲邵陵王，蜀郡王子文爲西陽王，廣漢王子峻爲衡陽王，臨海王昭秀爲巴陵王，永嘉王昭粲爲桂陽王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Prince Bao You of Nanping was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling; Prince Ziwen of Shu commandery as Prince of Xiyang; Prince Zijun of Guanghan as Prince of Hengyang; Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai as Prince of Baling; Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia as Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day jichou: Prince Bao You of Nanping became prince of Shaoling; Prince Ziwen of Shu became prince of Xiyang; Prince Zijun of Guanghan became prince of Hengyang; Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai became prince of Baling; Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia became prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁卯，詔曰：「軌世去奢，事殷哲后，訓物以儉，理鏡前王。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter, day dingmao, an edict said: "To bind the age to the past is to cast off excess; to serve the wise kings of old is to train the world in thrift and hold up their mirror to our own rule.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter, day dingmao, an edict said: "To bind the age to antiquity is to cast off excess; to serve the sage kings of old is to school the realm in thrift and hold their mirror to our own rule.

sentences.zh: 朕屬流弊之末，襲澆浮之季，雖恭已弘化，刻意隆平，而禮讓未興，侈華猶競。

translations.literal: We stand at the end of a drifting decadence and inherit a season of shallow drift; though We bow to Heaven and spread reform, striving with all Our heart for peace and plenty, courtesy and yielding have not yet risen, and rivalry in splendor still runs wild.
translations.idiomatic: We stand at the end of a drifting decadence and wear a season of shallow drift; though We bow to Heaven and spread reform, bending every effort toward peace and plenty, courtesy and yielding have not yet risen, and rivalry in splendor still runs wild.

sentences.zh: 永覽玄風，兢言集愧，思所以還淳改俗，反古移民。

translations.literal: Ever reading the way of the mysterious ancients, We are ashamed at every word; We mean to return the folk to purity, change custom, and move the people back toward the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Ever reading the way of the hidden ancients, We blush at every word We speak; We mean to return the folk to purity, change custom, and turn the people back toward the old ways.

sentences.zh: 可罷東田，毀興光樓。

translations.literal: The Eastern Fields may be abolished and the Tower of Rising Light torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Eastern Fields be abolished and the Tower of Rising Light torn down.

sentences.zh: 」幷詔水衡量省御乘。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued that the Water Balance office should measure and reduce the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered the Water Balance to measure and cut back the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 己卯，納皇太子妃褚氏，大赦。

translations.literal: Day jimao: the crown prince's consort of the Chu clan was received; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Day jimao: the crown prince took Lady Chu to wife; a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，班賜各有差。

translations.literal: From the princes and dukes downward, graded gifts were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down, graded gifts were handed out.

sentences.zh: 斷四方上禮。

translations.literal: Tribute gifts from the four quarters were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts sent up from the four quarters were halted.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉，詔曰：「舊國都邑，望之悵然。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dingyou, an edict said: "The old capital of a fallen state—merely to gaze upon it stirs longing.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day dingyou, an edict said: "The old capital of a fallen state—merely to look upon it stirs longing.

sentences.zh: 況乃自經南面，負扆宸居，或功濟當時，德覃一世，而塋壟欑穢，封樹不脩，豈直嗟深牧豎、悲甚信陵而已哉？

translations.literal: How much more when one has oneself faced south upon the throne and borne the screen at the imperial residence, or when one's merit saved the age and one's virtue steeped a whole generation—yet the mound and tomb are heaped with filth and the planted trees go untended: can the sigh be only as deep as the cowherd's at the frontier, the grief as sharp as Xinling's alone?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one has faced south on the throne and borne the screen in the imperial hall, or when merit saved the age and virtue steeped a generation—yet mound and tomb are choked with filth and the planted trees go untended: is the sigh to be only as deep as the cowherd's at the passes, the grief as sharp as Xinling's alone?

sentences.zh: 昔中京淪覆，鼎玉東遷，晉元締構之始，簡文遺詠在民，而松門夷替，埏路榛蕪。

translations.literal: In former days the central capital was overrun and the cauldrons and jade moved east; at the founding of Jin Yuan the people still carried Jianwen's songs, yet the pine gates fell to ruin and the roads to the mounds ran wild with brush.
translations.idiomatic: Once the central capital was overrun and the cauldrons and jade went east; at Jin Yuan's founding the people still sang Jianwen's lines, yet pine gates fell to ruin and the roads to the tombs ran wild with brush.

sentences.zh: 雖年代殊往，撫事興懷。

translations.literal: Though the years lie far apart, to touch such things is to stir the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though the years lie far apart, to touch such things is to stir the heart anew.

sentences.zh: 晉帝諸陵，悉加脩理，幷增守衛。

translations.literal: All the tombs of the Jin emperors shall be repaired in full, and their guard strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Every tomb of the Jin emperors shall be repaired in full, and guard doubled.

sentences.zh: 吳、晉陵二郡失稔之鄉，蠲三調有差。」

translations.literal: In Wu and Jinling commanderies, districts that lost the harvest shall have the three levies remitted in graded measure."
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Jinling, districts that lost the harvest shall have the three levies forgiven in graded measure."

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁卯，以陰平王楊炅子崇祖爲沙州刺史，封陰平王。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui, lord of Yinping, was made Inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as Prince of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, spring, first month, day dingmao: Yang Chongzu, son of Yang Gui of Yinping, was made inspector of Sha and enfeoffed as prince of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將建安王寶夤爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: North General of the Army Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an, north general of the army, took Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔申明守長六周之制。

translations.literal: Day jisi: an edict proclaimed afresh the six-year rule for prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Day jisi: an edict proclaimed afresh the six-year rule for prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔「去歲索虜寇邊，緣邊諸州郡將士有臨陣及疾病死亡者，竝送還本土。」

translations.literal: Day yiyou: an edict said, "Last year the northern foe raided the border; among officers and soldiers of the frontier commanderies and districts who died in battle or of illness, all are to be sent home to their native places."
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: an edict said, "Last year the northern foe raided the frontier; officers and soldiers of the border commanderies who fell in battle or died of illness are all to be sent home."

sentences.zh: 三月壬午，詔「車府乘輿有金銀飾校者，皆剔除。」

translations.literal: Third month, day renwu: an edict said, "Imperial carriages in the carriage office that bear gold or silver fittings are all to have them stripped away."
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day renwu: an edict said, "Every imperial carriage in the carriage office with gold or silver trim is to have it stripped away."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，虜寇司州，戍兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Fourth month of summer: the foe raided Sizhou; the garrison troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month of summer: the northerners raided Si; the garrison troops broke them.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，以征虜將軍蕭懿爲益州刺史，前軍將軍陰廣宗爲梁、南秦二州刺史，前新除寧州刺史李慶宗爲寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jisi: Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Yi was made Inspector of Yi; Vanguard General Yin Guangzong was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved as inspector of Ning, was again made Inspector of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Yi, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Yi; Yin Guangzong, vanguard general, took Liang and South Qin; Li Qingzong, newly relieved of Ning, was again made inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 秋九月辛酉，以冠軍將軍徐玄慶爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Ninth month of autumn, day xinyou: Champion General Xu Xuanqing was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month of autumn, day xinyou: Xu Xuanqing, champion general, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，以輔國將軍申希祖爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter: Supporter-of-the-State General Shen Xizu was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter: Shen Xizu, supporter-of-the-state general, took Si.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月戊寅，皇太子冠，賜王公以下帛各有差，爲父後者賜爵一級。

translations.literal: Intercalary twelfth month, day wuyin: the crown prince was capped; silk was granted to princes, dukes, and officials downward in graded measure; those who had succeeded their fathers were given one step in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary twelfth month, day wuyin: the crown prince came of age; princes, dukes, and officers down received graded gifts of silk; those who had succeeded their fathers were raised one rank.

sentences.zh: 斷遠近上禮。

translations.literal: Tribute gifts from near and far were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts sent up from near and far were halted.

sentences.zh: 又詔「今歲不須光新，可以見錢爲百官供給。」

translations.literal: Another edict said, "This year there is to be no seasonal refurbishment; ready cash may be used to supply the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "This year skip the seasonal refurbishment; pay the hundred officials in ready cash instead."

sentences.zh: 四年春正月庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: Fourth year, spring, first month, day gengwu: a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, spring, first month, day gengwu: a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「嘉肴停俎，定方旨於必甘；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Fine dishes may rest on the stand, yet the right flavor must be sweet in the end;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Fine dishes may rest on the stand, yet the right flavor must prove sweet at last;

sentences.zh: 良玉在攻，表圭璋於旣就。

translations.literal: good jade may lie under the chisel, yet the scepter-gem shows itself only when the work is done.
translations.idiomatic: good jade may lie under the chisel, yet the scepter-gem shines only when the shaping is done.

sentences.zh: 是以陶鈞萬品，務本爲先；

translations.literal: Therefore in shaping the myriad kinds, to hold to the root comes first;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in shaping the myriad kinds, to hold to the root comes first;

sentences.zh: 經緯九區，學斅爲大。

translations.literal: in ordering the nine regions, learning and culture are the greatest thing.
translations.idiomatic: in ordering the nine regions, learning and culture are the greatest thing.

sentences.zh: 往因時康，崇建庠序，屯虞薦有，權從省廢，謳誦寂寥，倏移年稔，永言古昔，無忘旰昃。

translations.literal: In former days, when the times were at ease, the school halls were raised in splendor; when hardship followed in turn, they were provisionally cut back; songs and recitation fell silent, and years heaped up before one knew it—yet to speak of the ancients is never to forget the lamp at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: In easier times the school halls were raised in splendor; when hardship came they were cut back for a season; song and recitation fell silent, and years piled up before one knew it—yet to speak of the ancients is never to forget the lamp at dusk.

sentences.zh: 今華夏乂安，要荒慕向，締脩東序，實允適時。

translations.literal: Now within the four seas there is peace, and the far marches turn their faces in longing; to bind and repair the Eastern Hall is truly fit for the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Now within the four seas there is peace, and the far marches turn their faces in longing; to bind and repair the Eastern Hall is truly fit for the hour.

sentences.zh: 便可式依舊章，廣延國胄，弘敷景業，光被後昆。

translations.literal: Let the old statutes be taken as model, the imperial kin widely enrolled, the bright enterprise spread abroad, and its light cast upon generations to come."
translations.idiomatic: Let the old statutes be taken as model, the imperial kin widely enrolled, the bright enterprise spread abroad, and its light cast upon generations to come."

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，詔「民產子者，蠲其父母調役一年，又賜米十斛。

translations.literal: Day renyin: an edict said, "When the people bear a child, their parents' levies and corvée are remitted for one year, and ten hu of grain are also granted.
translations.idiomatic: Day renyin: an edict said, "When the people bear a child, their parents' levies and corvée are forgiven for one year, and ten hu of grain are granted besides.

sentences.zh: 新婚者，蠲夫役一年」。

translations.literal: When they newly marry, the husband's corvée is remitted for one year."
translations.idiomatic: When they newly marry, the husband's corvée is forgiven for one year."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，尚書令王晏伏誅。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingchen: Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二月甲子，以左僕射徐孝嗣爲尚書令，征虜將軍蕭季敞爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, day jiazi: Left Vice Director Xu Xiaosi was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Suppressing-the-Barbarians General Xiao Jichang was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day jiazi: Xu Xiaosi, left vice director, became director of the masters of writing; Xiao Jichang, suppressing-the-barbarians general, took Guang.

sentences.zh: 三月乙未，右僕射沈文季領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Third month, day yiwei: Right Vice Director Shen Wenji also held the post of Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day yiwei: Shen Wenji, right vice director, also took protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，追尊景皇所生王氏爲恭太后。

translations.literal: Eighth month of autumn: the birth mother of the Revered Emperor, the Wang clan, was posthumously honored as the Reverent Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month of autumn: Wang, birth mother of the Revered Emperor, was posthumously honored as the Reverent Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 索虜寇沔北。

translations.literal: The northern foe raided north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners raided north of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，又寇司州。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter: they raided Sizhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter: they raided Si again.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遣太子中庶子梁王、右軍司馬張稷討之。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: Crown Prince Attendant-in-Ordinary the Prince of Liang and Right Army Major Zhang Ji were sent to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiaxu: the Prince of Liang, crown prince attendant-in-ordinary, and Zhang Ji, major of the right army, were sent against them.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，以氐楊靈珍爲北秦州刺史、仇池公、武都王。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingchen: the Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen was made Inspector of North Qin, Duke of Qiuchi, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day bingchen: Yang Lingzhen of the Di was made inspector of North Qin, duke of Qiuchi, and king of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔「所在結課屋宅田桑，可詳減舊價。」

translations.literal: Day dinghai: an edict said, "Tax assessments on houses, dwellings, fields, and mulberry lands in every district may be reviewed and the old valuations reduced in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Day dinghai: an edict said, "Tax rolls on houses, fields, and mulberry lands in every district may be reviewed and old valuations cut in detail."

sentences.zh: 十二月甲子，以冠軍將軍裴叔業爲豫州刺史，冠軍將軍徐玄慶爲徐州刺史，寧朔將軍左興盛爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jiazi: Champion General Pei Shuye was made Inspector of Yu; Champion General Xu Xuanqing was made Inspector of Xu; Pacifying-the-Barbarians General Zuo Xingsheng was made Inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day jiazi: Pei Shuye, champion general, took Yu; Xu Xuanqing, champion general, took Xu; Zuo Xingsheng, pacifying-the-barbarians general, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，遣度支尚書崔慧景率衆救雍州。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: Minister of Revenue Cui Huijing was sent at the head of the host to relieve Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingchou: Cui Huijing, minister of revenue, led the host to relieve Yong.

sentences.zh: 二月癸丑，遣左衛將軍蕭惠休假節援壽陽。

translations.literal: Second month, day guichou: Left Guards General Xiao Hui on leave of absence bore the staff and went to aid Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day guichou: Xiao Hui, left guards general on leave, bore the staff and marched to relieve Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 辛未，豫州刺史裴叔業擊虜於淮北，破之。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: Inspector of Yu Pei Shuye attacked the foe north of the Huai and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinwei: Pei Shuye, inspector of Yu, struck the northerners north of the Huai and broke them.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，平西將軍蕭遙欣領雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: Pacifying-the-West General Xiao Yaoxin also held Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinsi: Xiao Yaoxin, pacifying-the-west general, also took Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月丙午，蠲雍州遇虜之縣租布。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingwu: the land tax and cloth levies of Yongzhou districts that suffered the foe were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day bingwu: land tax and cloth levies were forgiven in Yong districts that suffered the raid.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「仲尼明聖在躬，允光上哲，弘厥雅道，大訓生民，師範百王，軌儀千載。

translations.literal: Day wushen: an edict said, "Zhongni's bright sagehood was in his person; he matched the highest wisdom, spread his elegant way, and greatly instructed the living folk; he was model to the hundred kings and measure for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Day wushen: an edict said, "Confucius bore bright sagehood in his person; he matched the highest wisdom, spread his elegant way, and greatly taught the living folk; he was model to the hundred kings and measure for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 立人斯仰，忠孝攸出，玄功潛被，至德彌闡。

translations.literal: To stand as men look up to him, loyalty and filial piety issue forth; his hidden merit spreads abroad, and his utmost virtue shines ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: Men look up to him and loyalty and filial piety flow from it; his hidden merit spreads abroad, and his utmost virtue shines ever wider.

sentences.zh: 雖反袂遐曠，而祧薦靡闕，時祭舊品，秩比諸侯。

translations.literal: Though sleeves are turned in grief across distant ages, the ancestral offerings have never lacked; the seasonal sacrifices of old keep rank equal to the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Though sleeves are turned in grief across distant ages, the ancestral offerings have never lacked; the seasonal rites of old keep rank equal to the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 頃歲以來，祀典陵替，俎豆寂寥，牲奠莫舉，豈所以克昭盛烈，永隆風教者哉！

translations.literal: In recent years the sacrificial canon has fallen into ruin; the stands and vessels stand empty, and the victim offerings go unraised—how can this display the full splendor of his merit and forever exalt his transforming teaching!
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the sacrificial canon has fallen into ruin; stands and vessels stand empty, and victims go unraised—how can this show the full splendor of his merit and forever exalt his teaching!

sentences.zh: 可式循舊典，詳復祭秩，使牢餼備禮，欽饗兼申。」

translations.literal: Let the old rites be taken as model; the sacrificial ranks be set out in detail, so that the pens are stocked and the rites complete, and reverent offering be fully restored."
translations.idiomatic: Let the old rites be taken as model; sacrificial ranks be set out in detail, so pens are stocked and rites complete, and reverent offering fully restored."

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲寅，改元，赦三署囚繫原除各有差。

translations.literal: Fourth month of summer, day jiayin: the era name was changed; prisoners of the three offices were pardoned and released in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month of summer, day jiayin: the era name was changed; prisoners of the three offices were pardoned and released in graded measure.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two steps in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers were raised two steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以鎮軍將軍蕭坦之爲侍中、中領軍。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: Suppressing-the-Army General Xiao Tanzhi was made Palace Attendant and Central Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingxu: Xiao Tanzhi, suppressing-the-army general, became palace attendant and central director of the army.

sentences.zh: 己未，立武陵昭王子子坦爲衡陽王。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: Prince Zitan, son of Zhaowang of Wuling, was established as Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiwei: Prince Zitan, son of Zhaowang of Wuling, was established as prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以西中郎長史劉暄爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Western General of the Army Chief Clerk Liu Xuan was made Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingyin: Liu Xuan, chief clerk of the western general of the army, took Ying.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，大司馬會稽太守王敬則舉兵反。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: Grand Marshal and Administrator of Kuaiji Wang Jingze rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingmao: Wang Jingze, grand marshal and administrator of Kuaiji, rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 五月壬午，遣輔國將軍劉山陽率軍東討。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renwu: Supporter-of-the-State General Liu Shanyang led the army east to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day renwu: Liu Shanyang, supporter-of-the-state general, led the army east against him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，斬敬則，傳首。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Jingze was beheaded and his head sent about.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: Jingze was beheaded and his head displayed.

sentences.zh: 曲赦浙東、吳、晉陵七郡。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to the seven commanderies of eastern Zhe, Wu, and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty ran through the seven commanderies of eastern Zhe, Wu, and Jinling.

sentences.zh: 以後軍長史蕭穎胄爲南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Rear Army Chief Clerk Xiao Yingke was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingke, rear army chief clerk, took South Yan.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以北中郎將司馬元和爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: North General of the Army Major Sima Yuanhe was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingyou: Sima Yuanhe, major of the north general of the army, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，以輔國將軍王珍國爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Seventh month of autumn: Supporter-of-the-State General Wang Zhenguo was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month of autumn: Wang Zhenguo, supporter-of-the-state general, took Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以太子中庶子梁王爲雍州刺史，太尉陳顯達爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Crown Prince Attendant-in-Ordinary the Prince of Liang was made Inspector of Yongzhou; Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: the Prince of Liang, crown prince attendant-in-ordinary, took Yong; Chen Xianda, grand commandant, took Jiang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝崩于正福殿，年四十七。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: the emperor died in the Hall of Correct Blessing, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiyou: the emperor died in the Hall of Correct Blessing, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：「徐令可重申八命。

translations.literal: His final testament said: "Director Xu may again receive the eightfold honor.
translations.idiomatic: His final testament said: "Director Xu may again receive the eightfold honor.

sentences.zh: 中書監本官悉如故，沈文季可左僕射，常侍護軍如故，江祏可右僕射，江祀可侍中，劉暄可衛尉。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, his original office, is all to remain as before; Shen Wenji may be Left Vice Director, with attendant-in-ordinary and protector of the army unchanged; Jiang You may be Right Vice Director; Jiang Si may be Palace Attendant; Liu Xuan may be Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the masters of writing—his original post—remains as before; Shen Wenji may be left vice director, with attendant-in-ordinary and protector of the army unchanged; Jiang You may be right vice director; Jiang Si may be palace attendant; Liu Xuan may be commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 軍政大事委陳太尉。

translations.literal: Military and state affairs are entrusted to Grand Commandant Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs are entrusted to Grand Commandant Chen.

sentences.zh: 內外衆事，無大小委徐孝嗣、遙光、坦之、江祏，其大事與沈文季、江祀、劉暄參懷。

translations.literal: All inner and outer affairs, great and small, are entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Yaoguang, Tanzhi, and Jiang You; great affairs are to be weighed with Shen Wenji, Jiang Si, and Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: All inner and outer affairs, great and small, go to Xu Xiaosi, Yaoguang, Tanzhi, and Jiang You; great affairs are to be weighed with Shen Wenji, Jiang Si, and Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 心膂之任可委劉悛、蕭惠休、崔惠景。

translations.literal: Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Hui on leave, and Cui Huijing."
translations.idiomatic: Tasks of the heart and sinew may be entrusted to Liu Jun, Xiao Hui on leave, and Cui Huijing."

sentences.zh: 」葬興安陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Xing'an Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Xing'an Tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝明審有吏才，持法無所借。

translations.literal: The emperor was clear-sighted and had the talent of an administrator; in holding to the law he showed favor to none.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was clear-sighted and had the talent of an administrator; in holding to the law he spared no one.

sentences.zh: 制御親幸，臣下肅清。

translations.literal: He controlled those the ruler favored, and his ministers were brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: He reined in the ruler's favorites, and his ministers were brought to order.

sentences.zh: 驅使寒人不得用四幅傘，大存儉約。

translations.literal: He drove and used men of humble birth and would not let them use four-panel umbrellas; he greatly preserved thrift.
translations.idiomatic: He drove men of humble birth hard and would not let them carry four-panel umbrellas; he held hard to thrift.

sentences.zh: 罷世祖所起新林苑，以地還百姓；

translations.literal: He abolished the New Forest Park that Shizu had built and returned the land to the people;
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the New Forest Park that Emperor Wu had built and returned the land to the people;

sentences.zh: 廢文帝所起太子東田，斥賣之；

translations.literal: he abolished the crown prince's Eastern Fields that Emperor Wen had built and sold them off;
translations.idiomatic: he abolished the crown prince's Eastern Fields that Emperor Wen had built and sold them off;

sentences.zh: 永明中輿輦舟乘，悉剔取金銀還主衣庫。

translations.literal: in the Yongming era all carriages and boats had their gold and silver stripped and returned to the master-of-garments storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: in the Yongming era all carriages and boats had their gold and silver stripped and returned to the master-of-garments storehouse.

sentences.zh: 太官進御食，有裹蒸，帝曰：「我食此不盡，可四片破之，餘充晚食。

translations.literal: When the Grand Kitchen presented imperial food with wrapped steam-cakes, the emperor said, "I cannot finish this; it may be broken into four pieces, and the rest kept for the evening meal."
translations.idiomatic: When the grand kitchen sent up wrapped steam-cakes, the emperor said, "I cannot finish this; break it into four and keep the rest for the evening meal."

sentences.zh: 」而世祖掖庭中宮殿服御，一無所改。

translations.literal: Yet in the inner palaces of Shizu not a single garment or fitting was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Shizu's inner palaces not a single garment or fitting was changed.

sentences.zh: 性猜忌多慮，故亟行誅戮。

translations.literal: By nature he was suspicious and full of cares, and therefore executions followed in quick succession.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was suspicious and full of cares, and therefore executions followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 潛通道術，用計數，出行幸，先占利害，南出則唱云西行，東遊則唱云北幸。

translations.literal: He secretly practiced the arts of the Way and used stratagems; when he went out on tour he first divined gain and loss—if he went south he would cry that he was going west, and if he toured east he would cry that he was going north.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly practiced the arts of the Way and used stratagems; before he went abroad he divined gain and loss—if he went south he cried that he was going west, and if he toured east he cried that he was going north.

sentences.zh: 簡於出入，竟不南郊。

translations.literal: He was sparing in going out, and in the end never performed the southern suburb rite.
translations.idiomatic: He was sparing in going out, and in the end never performed the southern suburb rite.

sentences.zh: 上初有疾，無輟聽覽，秘而不傳。

translations.literal: When he first fell ill he did not cease hearing cases, and kept it secret without announcement.
translations.idiomatic: When he first fell ill he did not cease hearing cases, and kept it secret.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾甚久，勑臺省府署文簿求白魚以爲治，外始知之。

translations.literal: When his illness had long been grave, he ordered the ministries and offices to search their documents for white fish to use as medicine, and only then did those outside learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness had long been grave, he ordered the ministries and offices to search their documents for white fish to use as medicine, and only then did those outside learn of it.

sentences.zh: 身衣絳衣，服飾皆赤，以爲厭勝。

translations.literal: He wore crimson robes, and all his ornaments were red, as a charm against ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He wore crimson robes, and all his ornaments were red, as a charm against ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 巫覡云：「後湖水頭經過宮內，致帝有疾。

translations.literal: Shamans and spirit-mediums said: "The headwaters of Rear Lake pass through the palace grounds, causing the emperor's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mediums said, "Rear Lake's source runs through the palace—that is why the emperor is sick.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃自至太官行水溝。

translations.literal: 」The emperor then went in person to the Grand Provisioner's drainage ditch.
translations.idiomatic: " He went himself to the Grand Provisioner's runoff channel.

sentences.zh: 左右啓：「太官若無此水則不立。

translations.literal: Attendants reported: "If the Grand Provisioner lacked this water it could not operate.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants warned, "Without that water the Grand Provisioner cannot function.

sentences.zh: 」帝決意塞之，欲南引淮流。

translations.literal: 」The emperor resolved to block it, intending to divert the Huai southward.
translations.idiomatic: " He set his mind to dam it and draw the Huai south instead.

sentences.zh: 會崩，事寢。

translations.literal: Before long he died; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He died first; the plan slept.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高宗以支庶纂曆，據猶子而爲論，一朝到此，誠非素心，遺寄所當，諒不獲免。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Gaozong took the succession as a collateral scion; commentators treat him as an adoptive son—once he reached this point it was hardly his original intent; what the testament entrusted, he surely could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Gaozong took the throne from a side branch; men judge him as a fostered son. To rise to this in a single stroke was never his first heart; what the dying charge laid upon him, he could hardly refuse.

sentences.zh: 夫戕夷之事，懷抱多端，或出自雄忍，或生乎畏懾。

translations.literal: As for killing and cutting down kin, the motives are many—some spring from bold ruthlessness, some from fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter of kin wears many faces—sometimes bold cruelty, sometimes terror.

sentences.zh: 令同財之親，在我而先棄；

translations.literal: Kin who shared the same inheritance he made cast off while he still held power;
translations.idiomatic: He cast off kinsmen of the shared patrimony before they cast him off;

sentences.zh: 進引之愛，量物其必違。

translations.literal: those he had advanced and drawn close, he weighed and knew must turn against him.
translations.idiomatic: favorites he had raised and pulled near, he read by their weight and knew they must break away.

sentences.zh: 疑怯旣深，猜似外入，流涕行誅，非云義舉，事苟求安，能無內愧？

translations.literal: Suspicion and timidity ran deep; mistrust seemed to come from without; he wept as he carried out executions—not called a righteous act; if one seeks only safety in the affair, how can there be no inner shame?
translations.idiomatic: Dread and doubt ran deep; every glance seemed an outsider's plot. He wept and killed—and no man called it justice. If a throne is held by fear alone, what night is free of shame?

sentences.zh: 旣而自樹本根，枝胤孤弱，貽厥不昌，終覆宗社。

translations.literal: Yet having planted his own root, branches and heirs were few and weak; he left decline to his line, and in the end overturned the ancestral state.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted his own line alone; branches thinned to a single weak shoot. What he left his sons was not flourishing fortune, but the fall of altar and realm.

sentences.zh: 若令壓紐之徵，必委天命，盤庚之祀，亦繼陽甲，杖運推公，夫何譏爾！

translations.literal: If the omens of a broken cord of succession had been surely entrusted to Heaven's mandate, then Pan Geng's sacrifice also continued Yang Jia's line; leaning on fate to advance the public good—what blame could attach?
translations.idiomatic: Had the cracked cord of succession truly been heaven's to mend, Pan Geng's rites would still have followed Yang Jia; when fate is the staff and the public good the path—what fault is there to name?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高宗傍起，宗國之慶。

translations.literal: In praise: Gaozong rose from a side branch—a blessing to the ancestral state.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Gaozong rose from the collateral line—a blessing to the royal house.

sentences.zh: 慕名儉德，垂文法令。

translations.literal: He cherished reputation and frugal virtue, and handed down text and law.
translations.idiomatic: He prized name and frugal conduct, and set writings and statutes down for later men.

sentences.zh: 兢兢小心，察察吏政。

translations.literal: Cautious and careful, scrutinizing the work of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wary and exacting, he peered into every corner of official business.

sentences.zh: 沔陽失土，南風不競。

translations.literal: Mianyang lost its soil; the southern wind could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Mianyang lost its lands; the southern power could not hold its own.
